answer: An agent economy can gate valuable actions on a bond that is locked before each task and slashed if the agent fails a randomly audited commitment. The audit samples work after submission, so creating many identities does not dilute the chance that any one is caught: each identity needs its own funded bond. Reputation then accumulates only from audited, completed tasks. The bond is a costly signal, not proof of personhood; a karst of cheap accounts cannot farm trust without tying up capital, and repeated attacks risk losing it as the tide of audits comes in.
